events.title: Edict of Milan Posted in Nicomedia
events.description: The agreement between Roman emperors Constantine the Great and Licinius, which called for benevolent treatment of Christians across the empire, was publicly posted in Nicomedia.
events.significance: The edict is widely seen as a turning point. It helped end the empire's persecution of Christians and set the stage for Christianity's rise in Europe.

events.title: Lewis and Clark Sight the Great Falls of the Missouri
events.description: The Lewis and Clark Expedition became the first European Americans to see the Great Falls of the Missouri River, in present-day Montana.
events.significance: The falls confirmed the explorers were on the right route. They also forced a grueling overland portage that tested the expedition.

events.title: Birth of W. B. Yeats
events.description: The Irish poet and dramatist William Butler Yeats was born in Dublin. He became a leading figure of the Irish literary revival and co-founded the Abbey Theatre.
events.significance: Yeats won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1923. He is remembered as one of the greatest English-language poets of the 20th century.

events.title: Battle of Villers-Bocage
events.description: Days after D-Day, German tank commander Michael Wittmann destroyed around 30 Allied vehicles in less than 15 minutes in the Normandy town of Villers-Bocage.
events.significance: The clash slowed the British advance in Normandy. It also became one of the most famous tank actions of World War II.

events.title: Miranda v. Arizona Decided
events.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled that criminal suspects must be told of their right to remain silent and to have an attorney before police interrogation.
events.significance: The ruling gave rise to the familiar "Miranda warning" and reshaped police procedure in the United States.
